title: Defamation — civil liability for injury to reputation

content.overview: Civil defamation protects reputation against false statements that tend to lower a person in the estimation of right-thinking members of society; liability turns on publication of defamatory matter referring to the claimant, subject to defences such as truth, fair comment, and privilege.
content.study: Separate civil tort from criminal defamation under the IPC/BNS. Prove defamatory meaning, reference to the claimant, and publication to a third party. Consider libel versus slander where the distinction still matters, and map defences: justification (truth), fair comment on matters of public interest, absolute and qualified privilege. Pair with negligence only where careless falsehood is framed outside classic defamation; keep the reputation analysis distinct.
